subject: Hosted API: Data geography + retention responses - FjordPay SQ
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fjordpay.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 16:12:00 +0100
Subject: Security questionnaire: Hosted API data residency & retention

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this. I'm attaching FjordPay's standard security questionnaire (redacted to the residency/retention section) — we need short, clear answers we can share with our legal and privacy teams. High level questions below to expedite:

- Where is customer request/response data stored at rest for the Hosted API? Any cross-border replication?
- What is the default retention window for requests, logs, and embeddings?
- Describe the deletion/erasure process and expected timelines for full customer data removal.
- Do backups or snapshots contain customer content? If yes, how long are they retained and what is the deletion process?
- Are there controls for region-pin (EU-only) for accounts in scope of GDPR?

We'd like a compact set of answers by Monday if possible. I've cc'd security@fjordpay.com and Liam O'Brien (privacy). Attachment: fjordpay-residency-questions.xlsx (see Q1-Q6).

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Vendor Security
FjordPay

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fjordpay.com>
Cc: security@fjordpay.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 17:38:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: Hosted API data residency & retention

Thanks Elaine — appreciate the clear scope. I'll cover the top-level answers here and loop in Kimberly for the operational details and evidence pack.

Short answers (high level):
- Primary storage: Customer request/response data for the Hosted API is stored in region-specific object stores and databases; for EU customers we deploy and store data in EU-hosted zones only (no automatic cross-border replication outside selected regions).
- Default retention: By default, transient request/response logs are retained 30 days; embeddings and derived artifacts are retained 90 days unless customer-configured retention policy says otherwise.
- Deletion: On customer erasure request we initiate a multi-step purge: immediate logical deletion from serving indices, followed by removal from primary stores and cache invalidation. Most customer-visible data is removed within 30 days; full removal from backups/snapshots can take up to 90 days depending on snapshot schedules.
- Backups: Backups/snapshots may contain customer data; retention windows are 90 days for incremental snapshots and up to 365 days for longer-term audit archives (long-term archives are scoped and require explicit enterprise agreement).
- Region pinning: Yes — we support account-level region pinning (EU-only) for hosted customers; we can provide an assurance matrix and routing policy doc.

I'm handing this to Kimberly to provide the operational descriptions, attachment(s) with the retention summary, and references to our audit artifacts.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Trust, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fjordpay.com>, security@fjordpay.com
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2028 09:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: Hosted API data residency & retention

Hi Elaine / team —

Thanks for the questionnaire. I've attached a concise "redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf" that maps our answers to the specific items in your sheet. Below are the operational details you asked for. I've tried to keep the answers short for your legal/privacy review.

1) Storage and cross-border replication
- Customer request/response payloads and associated metadata are stored in regional object stores and low-latency databases bound to the customer's chosen deployment region.
- For standard Hosted API accounts with EU region pin, we do not replicate content to non-EU zones. Replication to other regions occurs only when a customer explicitly enables multi-region failover (documented in the account settings and in our onboarding checklist).

2) Default retention windows (out-of-the-box)
- API request logs (access-level, not full payload replay): 30 days.
- Full request/response payloads (used for debugging/quality tooling unless customer opts out): 30 days.
- Embeddings and derived runtime artifacts: 90 days.
- Audit logs (system-level metadata): 365 days by default (can be shortened with enterprise contract).

3) Deletion / erasure process and timelines
- Step 1 — Logical delete (0–24 hours): We mark records as deleted and revoke access; any incoming reads will return 404/not found for deleted resources.
- Step 2 — Primary store purge (up to 30 days): Background jobs remove the deleted objects from primary stores and from the KV caches used by the serving runtime.
- Step 3 — Snapshot/backups purge (up to 90 days): Because snapshots are taken on a rolling schedule, data may persist in incremental backups; we remove the customer's logical entries from new snapshots and schedule scrub jobs to expunge older snapshots within a 90-day window.
- Step 4 — Long-term archive (if applicable): Data moved to audit archives (rare, opt-in) will follow the archive retention agreed in contract — typically only used with enterprise customers and subject to separate deletion timelines.

4) Backups and snapshots
- Backups are encrypted at rest and access-controlled. Incremental snapshots are retained for 90 days by default.
- For EU region-pinned accounts, snapshots are stored in EU data centers.
- In the event of an erasure request, we log the request and schedule scrub jobs; we will provide a confirmation when scrub completes.

5) Region pinning controls and evidence
- Account-level setting (Account > Data residency) restricts logical storage and snapshot storage to the selected region.
- We can provide an exported routing policy and a short evidence pack (audit snapshot and routing config) after appropriate NDA; see attached audits-2027-snapshot.zip (redacted).

6) Additional controls / encryption
- Data is encrypted at rest (customer-managed KMS available for Private deployments; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS with per-account keys).
- Transit encrypted via TLS 1.2+; we support mTLS for dedicated connections.

Attachments included in this reply: redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf (table mapping to your Qs), audits-2027-snapshot.zip (redacted evidence for region pin).

If you need exact phrasing for your SSA or a signed attestation for procurement, we can produce a short signed PDF.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Brien <liam.obrien@fjordpay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@fjordpay.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Jun 2028 16:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: Hosted API data residency & retention

Thanks Kimberly — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from privacy: can you confirm the confirmable SLA for customer-initiated erasure (we need language for our DPA) and whether there are any scenarios where data could be exported outside the EU without explicit customer consent?

On the SLA: Your note indicates visible data removed within 30 days and backups up to 90 days. For contracting we need a single-line commitment we can put in the DPA (e.g., "Redwood will complete logical deletion of customer content within X days and complete scrub of incremental backups within Y days"). Can you propose an agreed phrasing we can use?

On export: please confirm that for EU region-pin accounts you will not export customer content outside the EU unless the customer enables multi-region replication or there is a lawful request that compels transfer.

If you can send a one-line DPA-ready statement and confirm exports, we can close this section.

—Liam O'Brien
Privacy Counsel
FjordPay
